target.title: fix(agents): extend thinking error recovery to body, detail, and responseBody carriers
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closes #98368.

When an Anthropic provider returns a thinking-block error, the recovery detector in `wrapAnthropicStreamWithRecovery` (which strips thinking blocks and retries without them) only inspects a subset of carrier fields that commonly hold the error detail. The merged prerequisite (#98411) added `errorBody` coverage, but three additional carriers — `body`, `detail`, and `responseBody` — are frequently used by production wrappers (fetch-style responses, structured-error wrappers) and were still missed by the detector, leaving sessions to fail on recoverable errors.

## Changes

**Source** (3 lines): Added `current.body`, `current.detail`, `current.responseBody` to the candidate list in `shouldRecoverAnthropicThinkingError` (`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/thinking.ts`).

**Tests** (42 lines): Added 3 parameterized positive cases for the new carriers and a negative regression test verifying that non-thinking strings in these fields do not trigger false recovery.

**Scope:** 2 files, +45 lines. String-only carriers (no heuristic or serialization guard needed, unlike the deferred `data` path). Follows the same pattern as the existing `errorBody` carrier from #98411.

## Evidence

All tests pass; the three new positive table cases genuinely fail without the source change (the base error message carries no thinking token, so the carrier is the only match source):

```
Test Files  2 passed (2)
     Tests  104 passed (104)
```

The false-positive surface stays closed: only string candidates are pattern-tested, `content`/`text`/`data` are still never visited, `THINKING_BLOCK_ERROR_PATTERN` still requires the literal `thinking`/`redacted_thinking` token, and the one-attempt-per-session gate with `seen`-set dedupe is unchanged.
